# Codex review guidelines

## Mandatory engineering and review standards

These five rules apply to new and modified code. Untouched legacy code is not a reason to waive a rule on changed behavior. Read `.github/codex-review.md` during reviews and use `.github/pull_request_template.md` for PR evidence.

1. **No spaghetti or God functions.** Reject any new or modified function over 60 physical lines, callback/control nesting over three levels, or logic copied between Drive Mode, AV, Que → SUSPEND, Que → REQUEST, Reclass and Docks. Extract focused helpers with explicit inputs and outputs; do not compress statements onto one line to evade review. **Zero Monolith Growth:** Never grow a baseline file over 500 lines. **Mandatory Strangler-Fig Extraction Rule:** Whenever a task modifies logic in a legacy file over 500 lines, extract that domain slice into a focused ES module under 400 lines in src/core/, src/engine/, src/views/, src/ui/ or src/services/; the legacy file must strictly shrink. New or extracted modules must not exceed 400 lines anywhere. The committed baseline is immutable; after any committed shrink the immediately preceding size becomes the new ceiling for every later commit, index and worktree. Never reset upward or bypass it.
2. **Single source of truth.** Route row evaluation and published photo evidence through `publishRowEvaluationToMasterAndNotes`; route physical-row/card metrics through `resolveCanonicalInventoryRow` and its canonical hydration facade. Completion/MARK DONE state follows the matching durable receipt through `applyConfirmedRequestCompletionReceipt`. Existing subordinate authenticated upload transports retain their canonical owner. Reject one-off DOM/state patches, competing mutation owners and duplicate caches.
3. **Separation of concerns.** Keep Supabase SQL/RPC transport, state/commands and DOM rendering in separate owners. UI click/submit/change handlers dispatch commands; they do not issue raw database queries. Render only from canonical state and receipts.
4. **Supabase cost and quota guard.** Reject executable image-transformation requests under `/storage/v1/render/image/`, new unguarded interval/recursive timeout/realtime refresh loops and runtime references to any Supabase project except `kzrnyjsosryejjejliii`. Polling requires an explicit bounded interval, lifecycle/single-flight guards and failure backoff. Retain historical evidence and inert negative test fixtures; they must never become alternate production routes.
5. **Zero dead code.** Reject commented-out executable blocks, debug logs/debugger statements, unreachable branches, unused bindings, orphaned helpers and temporary workarounds. Keep required production telemetry and purposeful CLI/error output; neither is permission for debug logging or silent error suppression.

Mechanical enforcement: `node scripts/anti-spaghetti-lock.mjs` inspects new/modified first-party JS, TS, Apps Script and inline HTML scripts against Git history, including staged content separately. Its successful full validation writes an authenticated local proof bound to the exact worktree, index, Git history, guard code and parser dependencies; the fast hook rejects a missing, stale or altered proof. Rerun the full validation after staging or any input change. The canonical `scripts/fast-regression-lock.mjs` also retains all existing mutation, hydration, syntax, geometry and version contracts and its <2-second budget. Generated/vendor output is not an authoring surface. Reviewers must reject semantic duplicates, hidden network access, dead helpers or unsafe scheduling that a conservative static check cannot prove. No suppression comments, hook bypasses, force pushes or automatic baseline resets.

Cross-layer blast radius for this policy: development/review tooling and instructions only. Code.gs, SQL/RPCs, app-api, canonical runtime state, production data and published application assets retain their contracts.

Report concrete changed-line findings with severity, the violated invariant, the affected caller and the smallest safe repair. Require actual negative and safe-counterexample checks for guard changes. Do not call old debt a new regression; do not grandfather a modified oversized function. A passing static gate does not establish live email delivery, physical-device latency or complete semantic equivalence.
